ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Dorothea Lange

code.originalText: Endoscopy results and reflux treatment; post-polio syndrome follow-up

text.paragraph: Ms. Lange had an upper endoscopy two and a half weeks ago, three and a half weeks after her last omeprazole dose, under moderate sedation at reduced doses with oxygen and carbon dioxide monitoring and warming; she recovered without any fall in oxygen saturation. It showed Los Angeles grade B esophagitis and a 2 cm sliding hiatal hernia, with a regular junction and no Barrett's esophagus; the stomach showed healed changes of her ulcer operation and no ulcer, and the gastric biopsies showed no Helicobacter pylori. The fever and aching after the zoledronic acid infusion settled in three days. Heartburn continues on four or five nights a week on antacid tablets. Physical therapy ends next week; she has learned her home program. No falls. She is printing in the darkroom for an exhibition and photographing two days a week. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-05-18; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Strength unchanged: left quadriceps 4/5, right quadriceps 3+/5
Steady with the orthosis and cane; Timed Up and Go 11.5 seconds

New fatigue and slowly increasing weakness for about 18 months, in the left leg and both arms as well as the right leg weakened by polio at seven, with aching muscle pain after work and cold intolerance of the right leg; cause to be established
S — Synthetic presenting concern at the index visit, superseded by the diagnosis of post-polio syndrome at the second visit; the paralytic polio of 1902 is documented (D).

Post-polio syndrome (modified March of Dimes criteria met): new weakness of the left quadriceps and both shoulder girdles and increased weakness of the right leg, with fatigue, muscle pain, and cold intolerance, more than 50 years after paralytic polio with partial recovery and decades of stable function; nerve conduction normal; EMG chronic reinnervation in both legs and the right deltoid; other causes excluded

S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; the childhood polio is documented (D), and her biographer's account of post-polio symptoms later in life is a retrospective interpretation (R). No neurological finding from her lifetime is used.
Heartburn and regurgitation after meals and at night for three months, three to four times a week; no difficulty swallowing, weight loss, vomiting, bleeding, or anemia
S — Synthetic presenting symptom at the index visit, superseded by the endoscopic diagnosis at the fourth visit.
Gastroesophageal reflux disease with Los Angeles grade B erosive esophagitis on upper endoscopy off proton pump inhibitor; no Barrett's esophagus
S — Synthetic endoscopic diagnosis; it does not echo or foreshadow her later documented illness.
Small (2 cm) sliding hiatal hernia on upper endoscopy

Osteoporosis, worst at the right hip on the polio-weakened side (right femoral neck T-score -2.7; left -1.6; lumbar spine -1.8), with vitamin D insufficiency; no vertebral fracture on assessment; 10-year FRAX risk about 16 percent major osteoporotic and 4.5 percent hip
S — Synthetic bone density result; disuse of a polio-affected limb lowers bone density on that side.
Two falls in the past year without injury, from catching the right foot
S — Synthetic fall history at presentation.
Surgery for severe stomach ulcers in her early fifties; no ulcer symptoms since; avoids nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
S — Synthetic modern history entry linked to the documented ulcers and surgery of the late 1940s (D); the type of operation is not known.

Acute-phase reaction two days after the first zoledronic acid infusion: fever to 38.1 °C, muscle and joint aching, and headache, without signs of infection; calcium normal; resolved in three days with acetaminophen and fluids
S — Synthetic expected adverse effect of a first intravenous bisphosphonate dose.

list.item:
Reflux esophagitis, Los Angeles grade B (K21.00). Grade B esophagitis with typical symptoms that responded to a proton pump inhibitor establishes the diagnosis of reflux disease. There is no Barrett's esophagus, and she does not have the three or more risk factors that would call for Barrett's screening, so after this negative examination no surveillance endoscopy is needed. No Helicobacter pylori. [S]
Omeprazole 20 mg before breakfast for eight weeks to heal the esophagitis, then step down to the lowest dose that controls symptoms.
No meals within three hours of bed; raise the head of the bed; limit late wine and large evening meals.
Report difficulty swallowing, food sticking, weight loss, vomiting, or black stools at once.

Small sliding hiatal hernia (K44.9). Contributes to reflux; no treatment beyond the reflux measures. [S]
No surgery needed.

Post-polio syndrome (G14). Stable strength; pain 4 of 10; no falls. The infusion reaction did not affect her strength. [S]
Home exercise program four days a week after physical therapy ends.
Continue pacing and the orthosis.
